name: Sleep-spindle entrainment: burst-firing every 3 s in Stage 2 sleep
origin: Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009 (Laurentian University), one patient
summary: A burst-firing field of about 0.7 s once every 3 s through both temporoparietal regions while one patient dozed in a chair. In this one woman with epileptic-like experiences after a head injury, Persinger's lab reported that the onsets of Stage 2 sleep spindles correlated weakly (rho 0.30 to 0.40) with the field onsets over about seven minutes of recording. The 45 min here are this project's extension.
notes: The patient sat blindfolded in a chair in an acoustic chamber. Her EEG was recorded for 5 min without field, in which she showed Stage 2 spindles. Then the field was switched on; the analysis covers 440 s of it. The helmet had four solenoids per side, and each left-right pair was on for 0.5 s. Each pulse lasted 690 ms, with 3-ms points (Persinger 2009 p.3 [376]). This program plays 5 min without field, then 45 min of a 690-ms burst followed by a 3-s pause. The 45 min are this project's extension. 'Once every 3 s' is read as the pause between bursts, as the lab defines it elsewhere (Persinger 1999 p.3 [165]); this paper does not say. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: 'about 1 microTesla along the inside edge of the lateral sides of the helmet' (p.3 [376]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet's field model gives about 24 uT at the scalp, over ten times the paper's value. One patient, no sham, a weak correlation. Without an EEG you cannot know your sleep stage or see spindles. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not a sleep treatment. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes covered, in a quiet dark room, at a time when you doze off easily; an EEG headband is needed to see spindles at all. The original was a laboratory session in a chair, not a night in bed.
schedule: A single laboratory session in the original; no schedule was published. Compare with Blind (possibly sham) sessions.
source: Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Entrainment of stage 2 sleep spindles by weak, transcerebral magnetic stimulation in an "epileptic" woman, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374-382 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (burst-firing file: 230 points at 3 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Persinger 1999, Int J Psychophysiol 34:163-169 (burst-firing 1 s every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10576400/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
